memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Sacrifice the other lamb at twilight with the same grain offering and its drink offering as in the morning — a pleasing aroma, a food offering presented to the Lord. For the generations to come this burnt offering is to be made regularly at the entrance to the tent of meeting, before the Lord. There I will meet you and speak to you;" - Exodus 29:41-42 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God attaches a promise to the daily offering: "There I will meet you and speak to you." The sacrifice was never the point in itself. It was the appointed place where God had committed to meet with His people and speak to them. Atonement opened the door to conversation.

Notice how ordinary the setting is. Not a mountaintop encounter, not a dramatic vision, but the routine daily offering at the tent entrance, repeated morning and evening for generations. God promised to show up in the regular, appointed rhythm.

That is enormously encouraging for those of us whose spiritual lives feel unremarkable. We sometimes assume God meets people in extraordinary moments and that our ordinary devotion does not count. But God's promise was attached to the daily thing. Jesus said that whoever has His commands and keeps them loves Him, and He will show Himself to them (John 14:21). Keep showing up at the ordinary appointed place. That is precisely where God has promised to meet you and speak.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I expect to meet God in ordinary daily devotion, or only in dramatic moments?
Am I showing up regularly at the place where God has promised to meet me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You promise to meet Your people in the ordinary appointed place. Help me show up faithfully, expecting You to speak, even when nothing feels dramatic. Amen.
